drafts_today.text:
The part nobody puts in the before-and-after photo: a good share of GLP-1 weight loss can be muscle, and a lot of people regain much of the weight when they stop.

After 70, muscle is what keeps you steady on your feet.

So before the scale: protein at every meal, lift something twice a week, and have a plan for after.
drafts_today.video_tip: 15 seconds to camera: say the first line, then count the three habits on your fingers.

drafts_today.topic: FDA eye warning on GLP-1s, no panic
drafts_today.text:
The FDA just added a rare vision-loss warning (NAION) to Ozempic, Zepbound and other GLP-1 labels.

Rare is the key word. Not a reason to panic.

It is a reason to call your doctor right away about any sudden change in one eye, and to keep up your eye exams if you're over 60.
drafts_today.video_tip: 10 seconds: hold your reading glasses, say 'rare, but know the sign', then the one-eye line.

drafts_today.topic: Sensitive skin: one product at a time
drafts_today.text:
Sensitive skin rule: never start three new products in the same week.

Add one. Give it 5 to 7 days. If your skin's calm, add the next.

That's how you find out what's working, and what's making you sting.
drafts_today.video_tip: 12 seconds: three products on the counter, slide one forward, hold up a calendar or seven fingers, then slide the next.

drafts_today.topic: Liver health: no trial and error
drafts_today.text:
"Fix your fatty liver" lists are everywhere this week.

If your liver is already a medical issue, please don't start a new supplement, tea or "detox" because a post said so.

Take the bottle to your doctor or pharmacist first. Your liver isn't the place for trial and error.
drafts_today.video_tip: 10 seconds: hold up a supplement bottle, read the first line, end tapping the label.
